reference: Contract expectations use Bash's documented type/command resolution and help synopsis behavior. The synopsis is independently taken from the published loadable catalog (killall5|killall5 -SIG), with Bash short-help formatting documented in the Bash loadable metadata contract. No GNU killall5 CLI exists as an oracle; the SysV killall5 operation is process control and is deferred.
coverage: Executed coverage is Bash availability/help metadata only; no operational behavior is counted as a pass.
Bash identifies killall5 as a builtin with type -t.
Bash resolves killall5 by name with command -v when candidate PATH is empty.
Bash short help exposes the catalog synopsis for killall5.
exclusions: No matching GNU CLI oracle is available for killall5, so there are no parity cases.
The suite does not walk /proc or invoke killall5 operational options, including --dry-run.
No process signals are sent; operation behavior requires a future disposable PID namespace with a reviewed proc/signal mock or owned sacrificial processes.

cases.purpose: Bash type -t must classify the compiled loadable as a builtin.
Bash command -v must resolve the builtin by its command name without relying on an external executable in PATH.
Bash short help must publish the loadable catalog synopsis; the expected text comes from the catalog entry killall5|killall5 -SIG.
Verify read-only target selection and omit-list handling without enumerating the runner's process set.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable PID-namespace VM or reviewed /proc fixture adapter plus an independent selection oracle. Exercise --dry-run with synthetic entries covering caller-session and self exclusion, empty-cmdline kernel-thread exclusion, omitted PIDs, malformed/disappearing records, and eligible outside-session PIDs. This suite does not invoke the operation.

cases.purpose: Verify the broadcast signal selection, omit-list behavior, and failure handling without sending signals to the runner's process set.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable PID-namespace VM with a reviewed kill(2) interceptor or explicitly owned sacrificial children and an independent expected-call oracle. Verify default and named signal numbers, excluded session/self/omitted PIDs, and injected ESRCH/EPERM outcomes. Never target host or general runner processes; this suite does not invoke signal delivery.
